element: Artisan (Baek & Pradel, Automated Table Reproduction via Code Generation, ASE 2026)

UC1.note: Deliverable is a reproduction script, never a venue-format appendix document.

UC3.evidence: Sec 2.1, p2: "given a research paper p, a table t from p, and an artifact URL u, automatically generate a reproduction script s that reproduces t using the artifact."
UC3.note: The script is an executable link from one paper table to artifact commands/files, but only for numeric tables, so partial is right.

UC4.evidence: Sec 1, p1: "authors can use Artisan to check whether their prepared artifact is sufficiently well-packaged and well-documented to facilitate reproduction."
UC4.note: Debatable: authors get only a pass/fail signal per table (script or no script), never an itemized report of missing files/deps/instructions, and no standard S is involved; 0 holds but 1 is arguable.

UC5.evidence: Sec 4.6, p9: "By using Artisan, we encounter 20 inconsistencies between papers and their artifacts... it is ultimately up to a human expert to decide if there is indeed a bug, and if so, where the bug lies."
UC5.note: Current 0 is wrong: the rubric says detecting paper-artifact inconsistencies counts as at least partial, and this is an explicit contribution (RQ5, Table 4, 20 inconsistencies, 14/16 confirmed by authors), though not fully automated.

UC6.evidence: Sec 2.1, p2: "If the provided artifact is non-functional (e.g., an obsolete Dockerfile), s may fix it, so the table can still be reproduced." Footnote 1: "most artifacts do not include such scripts."
UC6.note: Debatable: Artisan generates new artifact code (a reproduction script, sometimes fixing broken artifact code) but requires A as input rather than generating from P alone, so at most partial; 0 is defensible if 'from P' is read strictly.

B1.evidence: Sec 1, p1-2: "First, authors can use Artisan to check whether their prepared artifact is sufficiently well-packaged... Second, evaluators of artifacts can use Artisan to automate an important part of the evaluation process"
B1.note: Current 4 is slightly high: the paper names four audiences with authors listed first and evaluators second, though the keywords and Table 1 frame it as artifact-evaluation tooling, so 4 is defensible.

B2.evidence: Sec 2.5.1, p4: "the output judge runs the submitted script in a fresh container environment and classifies the result into four categories"

B3.evidence: Sec 2.1, p2: "given a research paper p, a table t from p, and an artifact URL u"; Sec 4.2.3, p8: "55% of the steps are spent on exploration (grep, cat, and sed commands)"
B3.note: Both P (obfuscated target table) and A (downloaded artifact) are required inputs; the agent works mostly inside the artifact, so 4 is arguable, but the target comes from the paper.

B4.evidence: Sec 5.1, p10: "Artisan expects the outputs to exactly match the expected results and thus cannot reproduce nondeterministic results."
B4.note: Correctness criterion is exact match to the paper's table; ACM badges only select benchmark papers (Sec 3.3), they do not drive the tool.

B5.evidence: Sec 2.2, p2: "Otherwise, Artisan outputs the submitted reproduction script."; Sec 2.5.2, p5: method judge classifies into "Copied results", "Last-mile reproduction", "Full reproduction"
B5.note: The deliverable is executable code plus a categorical outcome, fitting neither pole; 3 (or 0 = not applicable) is reasonable, no prose report is produced.

disagreements: UC5: current 0, should be 1 because discovering paper-artifact inconsistencies is an explicit contribution (RQ5, Sec 4.6, Table 4: 20 inconsistencies, 14/16 author-confirmed) and the rubric says this counts as at least partial; it is human-assisted, not fully automated, so not 2.

UC6: current 0, arguably 1 because Artisan generates new artifact code (reproduction scripts that most artifacts lack, sometimes repairing obsolete Dockerfiles/buggy artifact code), though it needs A as input rather than generating from P alone.

B1: current 4, arguably 3 because the paper explicitly lists authors first, then evaluators, then reusing researchers as intended users (Sec 1); 4 remains defensible given the artifact-evaluation framing.
one_line_summary: LLM agent that, given a paper table and artifact URL, generates and container-verifies a reproduction script, with judges rejecting wrong outputs and copied-results shortcuts.
